recommendation: Reject all four options as stated. Keep patient-visible progress copy, avoid a prompt-wide filler deletion and a rushed gateway latest-first mode, and only ship a narrowly scoped explicit latest/late/end-of-day route into the existing late-search path after a platform-equivalent replay proves edge priority and a rendered terminal response. If that proof cannot finish before opening, leave v94 unchanged and require the owner to explicitly accept the known abandonment risk.
evidence: The 10:50 live trace records the latest-time patient turn, a filler response, raw_resolve=None, date_source=fallback, POST /availability -> 409, and final node n_miss_unread; the turn therefore reached search and failed after routing.

The earlier trace shows the same fallback-plus-409 signature but n_miss_unread emitted both a check message and an office referral, demonstrating unstable prompt-level recovery behavior across similar runs.

The v94 graph routes n_offer 'wants later in the day' to n_page_2 but also routes the broader 'wants a different day or time' to n_negotiate, whose successful exit goes to n_search; these labels overlap for a latest-time question.
n_miss_unread has only three exits: a newly named day/date/week/weekend to n_search, gives-up to decline, and timeout. A time-only answer or nudge has no explicit productive recovery edge.
The structure report counts 20 duplicated filler blocks, four availability webhook variants, seven recovery nodes, and nine extraction configurations, so prompt-wide edits have broad blast radius.
The gateway availability envelope pads to two slot objects specifically because absent JSON paths leave stale Bland variables; any new result ordering must preserve count and clearing semantics.
No supplied artifact documents Bland behavior for an empty generation or defines a gateway latest-first request/response contract.
assumptions: The owner's term D5 catch-all refers to the broad n_offer edge labeled 'wants a different day or time'; no literal D5 identifier appears in the supplied graph.
The diagnostic node and gateway timestamps reflect the same patient turn and the 409 routes through an ok != true edge to n_miss_unread.
Latest should mean latest available on the already selected date unless the patient explicitly changes the date; this needs owner confirmation before gateway implementation.
No undocumented Bland edge-priority mechanism guarantees that a newly worded specific edge wins over a broad competing edge.
unique_catches: The claim that the message did not route to search is contradicted by the observed availability POST; the missing-edge theory confuses successful webhook invocation with successful rendered completion.
Removing the filler sentence may leave a syntactically and behaviorally broken shared instruction that still says to 'say' removed copy and run a search.
n_miss_unread's escalation rule based on how many times it has asked competes with its global nudge filler rule, explaining office-punt versus promise-and-ghost without any graph change.

At least six other recovery nodes share n_miss_unread's narrow date-only productive exit: n_miss_empty, n_miss_thin, n_miss_unbookable, n_clarify, n_miss_time, plus the closely related n_date_conflict class.
A naive latest-first reversal can change slot numbering and therefore which appointment a patient's reply 1 or 2 selects, not merely presentation order.

The graph's day_part extractor already maps latest/end of day to late, so the missing capability is not simply vocabulary recognition; routing, date preservation, gateway result semantics, and rendering must agree.
risks_or_failure_modes: Prompt-wide filler removal causes empty or suppressed generations, prevents transition, or removes the only patient-visible progress response on synchronous n_negotiate/n_recheck webhook turns.
New latest edges overlap broad different-time edges and produce model-dependent routing, especially for negation, history, date-plus-time, typos, and multilingual phrasing.
A gateway latest-first shortcut reverses ordinary offer order, breaks relaxed/near or alternate-office selection, or mismaps slot 1/2 while preserving stale Bland variables.

Leaving v94 unchanged causes promise-and-ghost abandonment for common phrasings such as latest appointment, last appointment of the day, anything later, end of day, near closing, after work, and as late as possible.
Prompt-only changes cannot make n_miss_unread deterministic because its ask-again, filler-on-nudge, and escalate-after-two rules conflict and the model chooses among them from conversation context.
A route-only fix still fails if the gateway treats the latest-time turn as date-less fallback and returns 409, or if Bland never renders the webhook result.
A rushed fix at one offer node leaves equivalent behavior inconsistent at n_offer_2, n_offer_3, n_offer_near, and the six sibling recovery nodes.
proof_slots: Repeated route matrix at every offer node for latest/last/end-of-day/anything-later/after-work/date-plus-latest/negated/historical/typo/Chinese variants, recording exact node path.
One-node Bland empty-generation canary proving whether non-empty output is required and whether the following webhook/edge still executes.
End-to-end replay proving latest-on-selected-date returns a rendered offer or explicit no-match response, never filler-only, office-punt, or 409 parking.
Gateway fixtures proving count 0/1/2 clearing, stable slot numbering, selected-date preservation, latest ordering, relaxation behavior, and alternate-office provenance.
Nudge replay after failure proving 'Hello?' reaches a bounded recovery response instead of repeating the promise indefinitely.
